<action type="say">
For an afternoon flight around 3:30–4:00, it’s normal for the gate not to show very far in advance—especially at a smaller airport like Birmingham. Often, gates don’t appear on boards or online until 60–90 minutes before departure, sometimes even closer if the inbound aircraft is still turning around.

As long as:
- The flight shows as “On time” or just “Scheduled” on AA’s site, and  
- There’s no big delay or cancellation notice,  

you don’t need to be worried yet.

Since you’re using a browser, here’s the quickest way to check:

1. Go to: https://www.aa.com/travelInformation/flights/status  
2. Enter:  
   - From: Birmingham, AL (BHM)  
   - To: Dallas/Fort Worth, TX (DFW)  
   - Date: today  
   - Time: “Afternoon” (if it gives time options), or use the flight-number search with AA 1234  
3. Look for:  
   - Status: “On time,” “Delayed,” “Cancelled”  
   - Gate: It may still say something like “—” or “TBD” until they assign it.

Rule of thumb:
- If you’re within ~1 hour of departure and there’s still no gate listed anywhere, check with an American agent or help desk—they’ll know if it’s a late gate assignment or if there’s a disruption.
- If you’re more than 1–2 hours out, “no gate yet” is usually just normal operations.

If you tell me exactly what status you see on that AA status page (Scheduled/On time/Delayed and any time changes), I can help interpret how likely it is to move, and how quickly you should head toward security or a particular concourse.</action>

<action type="say">
“On time” with a blank gate is generally not a bad sign—it usually just means the gate hasn’t been assigned or published yet, not that there’s a problem.

Typical timing:
- More than ~90 minutes before 3:45 pm: totally normal to have no gate yet.
- Around 60 minutes before: gate often appears, but it can still be blank if they’re waiting on the inbound aircraft or a gate to free up.
- Inside ~30–40 minutes: if it’s still blank everywhere, that’s when I’d walk to an American counter or any AA gate and ask—agents will see the assignment (or any issue) before the public boards sometimes.

What to do now:
- Keep that AA status page open in your browser and refresh every 10–15 minutes; AA’s own site usually shows the gate before the big terminal monitors.
- Once a gate shows up there, head that way and aim to be nearby at least 30–40 minutes before departure.

If you tell me roughly what time it is locally right now, I can say more clearly whether you’re still in the “totally normal” window or in the “go ask an agent” window.</action>
